title: Define staged admission flow and sanity-suite for new open model entries
creator: Marco Gonzalez
description:
Problem: New community/open model entries are landing in the catalog in varying states of readiness. Current onboarding guidance often forces a binary decision: fully pinned (operational burden) or unpinned (user risk). We need a lightweight, staged admission flow + a minimal automated sanity-suite to reduce both false positives during intake and engineering overhead for every new variant.

Goal: Define the PRD-level acceptance criteria, decision gates, and a 3-stage onboarding flow (intake, probation, graduated available) and the associated mandatory sanity checks that the runtime and console teams can implement. Deliverable: a concise, actionable spec that engineering can implement in a sprint, and PM/design signoff for UX changes in the console intake UI.
scope_inclusions: Minimal metadata schema required at intake (model size, float/quant formats, tokenizer id, compatible runtime tags)
Automated sanity-suite: basic generation smoke test, KV cache memory check, perf profile (short seq length), deterministic vs nondet check on small prompts
Decision rules for lightweight pinning (soft-pin + fallback mapping)
Console UX text/flags for staged status and expiration dates
Acceptance criteria for moving from probation -> graduated
scope_exclusions: Comprehensive performance benchmarking across 8 production workloads
Full model weight audit (security/legal) - separate intake step handled by security/compliance
Retroactive conversion of all previously onboarded community models
acceptance_criteria: A clear 3-stage flow is documented and approved by PM, Eng, and Design
Sanity-suite defined as a minimal set of 6 automated checks with pass/fail semantics
Sanity-suite outputs map to admission gates (block/probation/allow) and are stored in model metadata
Console reflects staged state with tooltip guidance and a link to the acceptance report
Runtime routing will honor soft-pinning: probation variants may be used for low-volume non-critical routes only
A migration plan exists to handle incidents caused by graduated models (rollback and unpublish steps documented)
Open-model intake template (JSON) published and validated by the intake form with schema validation
rollout_plan: Week 1: Socialize PRD with Eng + Design; finalize acceptance checks
Week 2: Eng implements sanity-suite hooks and metadata fields; console adds staged badge UI
Week 3: Pilot 3 community models through the flow; collect telemetry and adjust thresholds
Week 4: Iterate on UX copy and decision thresholds, prepare rollout announcement and docs
test_plan: Automated sanity-suite runs on PR model submissions and writes status to model-catalog-db
Create synthetic smoke prompts for generation quality (toxicity, hallucination heuristics) limited to probation classification
Load a burst of short-seq inference requests to validate KV/cache memory path under mocked traffic
E2E test: submit intake JSON via console -> sanity-suite -> console shows probation -> promote to graduated and verify routing respects soft-pin
migration_and_rollback_criteria: Graduated model causes >2% error-response increase or latency regression >25% on key charts -> automatic rollback to previous stable variant
Major safety/toxicity flag from monitoring -> immediate unpublish and incident review
Manual rollback steps documented with owner roles and communication templates
open_questions: What threshold values should trigger probation vs block for perf regressions? (Eng to propose initial thresholds)
Should probation variants be visible in catalog search by default or hidden behind an advanced toggle? (Product/Design decision)
How long is the probation window by default (30d suggested) and who can shorten/extend it?
Are we comfortable with 'soft-pinning' semantics where probation variants are allowed for ad-hoc tests but not for SLA-backed routes?
